promptLatex: Which proof strategy is most appropriate for proving 'for every integer $n \ge 1$, $2^n > n$'?
hintLatex: A claim quantifying over all natural numbers invites induction.
Inductive step: assume $2^k > k$, then $2^{k+1} = 2 \cdot 2^k > 2k \ge k + 1$ for $k \ge 1$.
solutionLatex: Proof by induction. Base case $n = 1$: $2^1 = 2 > 1$. Inductive step: assume $2^k > k$ for some $k \ge 1$. Then $2^{k+1} = 2 \cdot 2^k > 2k$, and $2k \ge k + 1$ because $k \ge 1$. Hence $2^{k+1} > k + 1$. By induction the claim holds for every $n \ge 1$.
